g1.label: 1. Aisha ___ home when she remembered
g1.why: A longer action in progress when something happened uses the past continuous: ‘was cycling’.

g2.label: 2. She suddenly ___
g2.why: A short, completed action uses the simple past: ‘remembered’.

g3.label: 3. Her cousins ___ in the garden
g3.why: An action already in progress when she arrived uses the past continuous: ‘were playing’.

g4.label: 4. The smell ___ through the window
g4.why: A background, ongoing action uses the past continuous: ‘was drifting’.

g5.label: 5. As she ___ into the room...
g5.why: A short, completed action uses the simple past: ‘stepped’.

g6.label: 6. Her grandmother ___ out of the kitchen
g6.why: A short, completed action uses the simple past: ‘came’.

g7.label: 7. While the family ___ together
g7.why: A background action happening at the same time uses the past continuous: ‘were eating’.

g8.label: 8. The sun ___ while she cycled home
g8.why: A background, ongoing action uses the past continuous: ‘was shining’.

g1.label: 1. Before that day, Aisha ___ jeans there
g1.why: An action true before an earlier point in the story uses the past perfect.

g2.label: 2. Earlier that week, she ___
g2.why: An action completed before the main story time uses the past perfect.

g3.label: 3. She realised she ___ about the lunch
g3.why: An earlier action revealed later in the story uses the past perfect.

g4.label: 4. She ___ that her aunts were visiting
g4.why: A fact true before the main story event uses the past perfect.

g5.label: 5. She was sure she ___ everything
g5.why: An earlier belief about a past action uses the past perfect.

g6.label: 6. She ___ to make a good impression
g6.why: A motive that existed before the main story event uses the past perfect.

g7.label: 7. By the time lunch ended, Aisha ___
g7.why: ‘By the time’ signals an action completed by a later past point, so the past perfect is used.

g8.label: 8. Her grandmother ___ about the jeans
g8.why: Consistent with the past-perfect backstory frame used throughout this narrative.
